metadata.note: Southern Pacific's Sunset Route, the second American transcontinental link (after the 1869 Overland Route -- see first_transcontinental_railroad.geojson), completed Feb 5 1883 when SP's Texas and Louisiana lines joined its existing California network, giving through New Orleans-Los Angeles service via Houston, San Antonio, Del Rio, El Paso, and Tucson. SP inaugurated its flagship named train, the Sunset Limited, in November 1894 -- it is generally cited as the oldest continuously operating named train in the United States. Unlike the other historical lines added to this map, this corridor does NOT disappear: Amtrak took over operation in 1971 and still runs the Sunset Limited today (see amtrak.geojson's 'Sunset Limited' feature, which picks up in 1971), so this file's coverage intentionally ends in 1971 as a hand-off rather than a discontinuation. Geometry is reused directly from amtrak.geojson's GTFS-derived 'Sunset Limited' shape (489 points) rather than hand-picked town waypoints, since Amtrak's route runs on essentially the same physical right-of-way the SP built in 1883 -- this is far more accurate than an approximation (an earlier hand-picked-waypoint version of this file incorrectly cut across the Rio Grande into Mexico between Del Rio and Sanderson; the real, GTFS-derived alignment correctly hugs the US side of the canyon there).
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunset_Route (New Orleans-Los Angeles completed Feb 5 1883 via consolidation of SP's Texas/Louisiana and California lines; second US transcontinental route)
https://www.history.com/this-day-in-history/february-5/southern-pacific-railroad-completes-sunset-route (first through passenger trains left New Orleans and San Francisco Feb 5 1883)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunset_Limited (named train inaugurated November 1894, generally cited as the oldest continuously operating named train in the US; Amtrak took over 1971)

https://www.american-rails.com/sunset.html (SP-era timetable: 42-hour New Orleans-Los Angeles schedule over 1,995 miles in the later Southern Pacific era, ~50mph average; 1926 timetable shows 71hr40min New Orleans-San Francisco)

data/amtrak.geojson 'Sunset Limited' feature (GTFS-derived shape, reused here on the premise that the physical New Orleans-Los Angeles right-of-way is essentially unchanged since SP's 1883 Sunset Route)
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Exact 1883-1894 pre-named-train schedule/frequency (estimated); precise speed progression across the SP era before the sourced later-era 42-hour figure; whether the specific alignment differed in any minor way from today's Amtrak-era track (realignments, cutoffs, or abandoned segments over 140+ years are possible but not checked here).
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
